reply: not beat. My last evaluated variant reached 7.5e-5. A linear fit with a t-class × P-basis reached about 8e-7, but it needs 20 terms, so it is not a closed form. The remaining structure appears to involve t-exponents near 0, ½, 1 and 3/2 together with a non-polynomial P-dependence (e.g. e^{-P}-type).

import numpy as np
def equation(t, P, params):

            - params[5]*t*P - params[6]*t**params[7]*P*np.exp(-params[8]*P) - params[9]*np.sqrt(t)*np.exp(-P))
